Examples

Turtle for the jobs people actually turn up with, then the ontology's own examples for every term that has one.

Worked examples

Every snippet below assumes these prefixes.

@prefix :     <https://example.org/> .
@prefix loze: <https://loze-ontology.org/> .
@prefix owl:  <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .
@prefix rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
@prefix xsd:  <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .

Give an event a time

You have an interview, and you want to say when it happened. Make :Interview a subclass of loze:Eventuality — you want the domain class — and every loze property that takes an eventuality still reaches it, because rdfs:domain is inherited. The time is a period of time, and loze:atTime joins the two.

:Interview
    a owl:Class ;
    rdfs:subClassOf loze:Eventuality .       # your class, under loze's category

:interview-delivery-team
    a :Interview ;
    rdfs:label "Interview with the delivery team" ;
    loze:hasAgent       :lance ;             # who ran it
    loze:hasParticipant :sam ;               # who else was there
    loze:hasTopic       :the-migration ;     # what it was about
    loze:atTime         :morning-2026-08-14 .

:morning-2026-08-14
    a loze:PeriodOfTime ;
    loze:hasTemporalCoordinate "2026-08-14T10:00:00"^^xsd:dateTime ;
    loze:hasDuration           "PT90M"^^xsd:duration .

Say when something started and stopped

loze:atTime says an eventuality was going on then — it need not cover the whole span. For the ends, use loze:fromTime and loze:untilTime.

:Migration
    a owl:Class ;
    rdfs:subClassOf loze:Eventuality .

:the-migration
    a :Migration ;
    loze:fromTime  :2026-q1 ;
    loze:untilTime :2026-q3 ;
    loze:atTime    :2026-q2 .    # still running in Q2

:2026-q2
    a loze:PeriodOfTime ;
    loze:isSubperiodOf :year-2026 .

Say who did what, to whom, with what

Rather than a bespoke relation per kind of event, loze gives you one set of roles that works across domains. Reach for these before inventing your own.

:Payment
    a owl:Class ;
    rdfs:subClassOf loze:Eventuality .

:payment-8871
    a :Payment ;
    loze:hasAgent      :acme-ltd ;       # the one who acts
    loze:hasRecipient  :supplier-ltd ;   # the one it is conferred on
    loze:hasInstrument :card-4417 ;      # the means
    loze:atTime        :2026-08-14 .

Describe a model, not a unit

The car model has an advertised weight; your car has a weight you could put on a weighbridge. They are different facts about different things. Make the model a schematic particular and it can carry its own data without becoming a class.

:ToyotaCorolla
    a loze:SchematicParticular .

:CorollaHatchback
    a loze:SchematicParticular ;
    loze:isDeterminationOf :ToyotaCorolla ;   # the counterpart of subclassing
    :advertisedWeight      "1205"^^xsd:decimal .

:my-corolla
    a loze:ConcreteParticular ;
    loze:isConcretizationOf :CorollaHatchback .

Say something general, without punning

This is what the category is for. A schematic particular is repeatable like a class but carries data like an instance, so a general fact about the model is an ordinary triple. The usual alternatives are a pun — one name used as both a class and an individual — or a restriction.

# The usual way. :ToyotaCorolla is a class so units can be instances of it,
# and an individual so it can hold a weight. OWL 2 permits the pun; nothing
# keeps the two in step, and the weight is invisible to a query over cars.
:ToyotaCorolla a owl:Class ;
    rdfs:subClassOf :Car .
:ToyotaCorolla :advertisedWeight "1205"^^xsd:decimal .   # the pun
:my-corolla a :ToyotaCorolla .

# loze. One entity, no pun. It is a particular, so the general fact is just
# a triple, and ?m a :Car / ?m :advertisedWeight ?kg both match it.
:ToyotaCorolla a loze:SchematicParticular, :Car ;
    :advertisedWeight "1205"^^xsd:decimal .
:my-corolla loze:isConcretizationOf :ToyotaCorolla .

loze is a top-level ontology after E. J. Lowe's four-category ontology, with Zemach's schematic particulars. Every term here is identified by an IRI under https://loze-ontology.org/.
